_readme: Ground truth OpenStreetMap does not have. Edit by hand, then re-run:
Every entry is located by a lat/lng point, snapped to the nearest path and
applied to that WHOLE path — a locked gate or a dead lamp affects the stretch,
TO COLLECT COORDINATES: open the site, turn on 'Inspect', click a path. It
names the path and copies a ready-to-paste JSON line to your clipboard.
Set "enabled": false on any row to keep it in the file without applying it.
_blocked_help: Paths nobody can walk: a wall, permanently locked gate, construction, or a
route that only exists on the map. Removed from the graph BEFORE the exposure
model runs, so foot traffic reroutes the way people really go.
_restricted_help: Paths that exist but are not open to everyone — staff-only service roads,
the inside of a hostel block you do not live in, faculty parking.
`who` is free text for the UI. Routing treats these as a heavy penalty
rather than removing them, because they ARE walkable for some people.
_timed_help: Paths that close after a certain time — the single most campus-specific thing
here, and the thing no generic map knows. `opens` and `closes` are 24h HH:MM.
A path with closes 22:00 is unusable on an 11pm walk, which is exactly when
_lighting_help: Surveyed lit/unlit ground truth. Outranks both the OSM tag and our seeded
estimate, and carries a much stronger prior than a citizen report — somebody
_landmarks_help: Places OSM is missing. `kind` is 'hostel' (people start here) or 'dest'
(people walk to here). Adding one changes the exposure model, because it adds
_emergency_help: Security posts, the medical centre, warden offices. Shown on the map and used
to tell a walker what help is near their route.
